kramamukti
(‘gradual release or लिबेरतिओन्’)
------------------------------------------
All systems of Hindu philosophy, especially the Vedānta, posit मोक्ष or लिबेरतिओन् from transmigratory existence as the final goal of life.
This मोक्ष or मुक्ति is of two types: sadyomukti (instant release) and क्रममुक्ति (gradual release).
When the aspirant, following the path of ज्ञान or knowledge, realises the आत्मन् (his Self), he attains sadyomukti or लिबेरतिओन् here and now. This is also called ‘jīvanmukti’ or लिबेरतिओन् even while living in this body. After the prārabdha-कर्म is exhausted and the body falls, he gets final लिबेरतिओन्, called ‘videhamukti’.
However, if the sādhaka combines the performance of actions ordained by the scriptures with devatopāsanā or meditation on gods like इन्द्र, he will go, after death to the ब्रह्मलोक (or सत्यलोक), the world of ब्रह्मा, by the path of देवयान (the path of gods, also called arcirādimārga or the path of light), live there till the dissolution of that world and then will get merged in the Supreme ब्रह्मन्. This is called ‘kramamukti’ or ‘gradual लिबेरतिओन्’.

krāntās
(‘[earth] hallowed by’)
------------------------------------------
Literally the word ‘krānta’ means ‘stepped upon or occupied’. In a more general way, it means a division. Some of the tāntrik works like the Mahā-siddhasāra Tantra have divided Bhārata-varṣa (greater India) into three क्रान्तास् or units, viz., viṣṇukrāntā, rathakrāntā and aśvakrāntā. The land to the east of the विन्ध्य hills, extending upto जाव is viṣṇukrāntā. The country north of the Vindhyas including Mahācīnā, is रथ-krāntā. The rest of the country westward is aśvakrāntā.
The three words are also used as adjectives to the earth in the Mṛttikāsūkta of the Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad (1.37). Before performing a Vedic sacrifice, the place has to be sanctified by running a horse-drawn chariot over the ground. Thus the earth becomes ‘krāntā’ or sanctified by the aśvas (horses) and the रथ (chariot). It is viṣṇukrāntā since it was stepped upon by the foot of विष्णु in his वामन-त्रिविक्रम इन्चर्नतिओन्. Since this earth, through the sacrifice performed there, gives ‘vasu’ or wealth in course of time it can also be called ‘Vasundharā’ (one who bears wealth).
